claim: Naive chimpanzees acquired a sequential puzzle-box skill socially after failing to innovate it during a preceding three-month baseline.
notes: Supports O3; does not establish open-ended cumulative culture.

claim: Observer bumblebees learned a two-step box solution from demonstrators after naive bees failed despite extended exposure.
notes: Strong counterexample to treating socially acquired non-reinnovatable skill as human-unique.

claim: Young honey bees without normal tutor exposure showed persistent dance errors, supporting a social-learning component in signal development.
notes: Communication learning; not equivalent to language.

claim: Geographic variation in pandanus tool design has been interpreted as compatible with cumulative change, though transmission mechanisms remain debated.
notes: Important contested case; inherited action patterns and individual learning are alternative contributors.

claim: Juveniles take more than a year to reach adult pandanus-tool proficiency and have opportunities to learn from parents and artifacts.
notes: Supports scaffolded development; does not prove high-fidelity imitation.

claim: Goffin cockatoos can socially acquire tool-use competence and some observers subsequently manufactured tools.
notes: Transmission appears more consistent with emulation than exact imitation.

claim: Goffin cockatoos innovated a composite tool solution requiring coordinated use of two objects.
notes: Shows sophisticated embodied problem solving outside primates.

claim: Wild female elephant rumbles differed by population and subtly by social group; social group predicted call similarity better than genetic relatedness.
notes: Suggests learned vocal variation; authors do not claim definitive proof of vocal production learning.

claim: Across cetaceans, encephalization covaried with social structure and brain size predicted breadth of social/cultural behaviours.
A 2025 perspective argues cumulative change and high-fidelity transmission are not uniquely human and proposes open-endedness as the stronger distinction.
notes: Defines the target hypothesis rather than supplying a species-level measurement.
